slides.0.title: The legal framework
slides.0.subtitle: A new law arrives, and the old rules stay
slides.1.title: The first system (1957–1975)
slides.1.highlights.0.title: The 1957 decree
slides.1.highlights.0.content: A decree of 10 January 1957 regulated appellations of origin for wines, liqueur wines and spirits
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Decree 58-223
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Dated 18 September 1958, it set the general conditions for AOC rules. The two Muscat appellations were defined the same day
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Two texts from 1975
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Law 75-10 of 19 February 1975 organises the wine sector and is the basis for planting permits. An order of 23 September 1975 classified the "zones viticoles"
slides.1.content: The system follows the French AOC model: a decree sets the framework and orders define each region.
slides.2.title: Law 99-57 of 1999
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Covers all farm products
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Dated 28 June 1999, it governs AOCs and indications of source for farm products. It covers not only wine but also olive oil and figs
slides.2.highlights.1.title: The minister delimits
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Article 5: the area is delimited by order of the Minister of Agriculture, which also sets production methods and the product's nature and characteristics
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Specifications and registration
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Article 10 requires producers to follow a cahier des charges. An approved application is published in the official journal, and if there is no objection within six months it goes into the official register
slides.2.content: The new law puts wine into a system shared by all farm products.
slides.3.title: Why the old rules still apply
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Article 37
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Law 99-57 repealed the 1957 decree, but the texts made under it stay in force until replaced under the new law
slides.3.highlights.1.title: What the 2001 order cites
slides.3.highlights.1.content: An order of 27 February 2001 still cites Decree 58-223 and the AOC orders of 1958 to 1989, so the wine appellations still rest on orders from the old system
slides.3.highlights.2.title: The limits of this course
slides.3.highlights.2.content: The full texts of the individual AOC orders are not online, so this course does not teach each region's grapes, yields or alcohol levels
slides.3.content: Reading Tunisian rules means reading the new law and the old orders still in force side by side.
slides.4.componentProps.slide.title: 🧠 Knowledge check
What does Law 99-57 cover?
A. Wine only
B. Spirits only
C. Exports only
D. AOCs and indications of source for all farm products
AOCs for olive oil and figs are registered under it too.
Under Law 99-57, who delimits an area?
A. The Minister of Agriculture, by order
B. The producers announce it themselves
C. Parliament, by separate laws
D. An international body
Article 5.
How does article 37 of Law 99-57 treat the old system?
A. Only the Muscat rules survive
B. It repeals the 1957 decree, but its implementing texts stay in force until replaced
C. Everything lapses at once
D. The old system stays forever
That is why the 2001 order still cites the 1958 decree.
How long is the objection period after an AOC application is published?
A. Two years
B. There is none
C. Six months
D. One month
Article 14: only without objection does it enter the register.
